## Development Guidelines

### Code Quality

- Formatting and linting are handled by [Biome](https://biomejs.dev/) (`biome.json`),
  not ESLint or Prettier. Use `bun ff` to format, lint, and check in one pass.
- Run focused tests, then the build-free `bun check:changed` gate before every
  push. `bun validate` is not run on agent machines because its Turbo graph can
  build workspace dependencies; it and app builds run in CI for the exact commit
  (see [pre-push checks](/build/development-tools/pre-push-checks)).
- Default to Server Components in `apps/web`; add `'use client'` only for state,
  browser APIs, or interactivity.
- Prefer typed expected errors and dependency services via `@tuturuuu/utils/effect`
  for new server/service orchestration.

### Git Workflow

- Use [Conventional Commits](/build/development-tools/git-conventions) for commit
  messages and branch names.
- The branch checker only accepts these prefixes: `feature/`, `feat/`, `fix/`,
  `bugfix/`, `hotfix/`, `release/`, `chore/`, `docs/`, `style/`, `refactor/`,
  `perf/`, `dependabot/`, and `claude/`.
- Keep commits atomic and write descriptive PR descriptions.
- Run `bun check:changed` before every push; it maps changed paths to the cheap
  CI gates without builds. See [pre-push checks](/build/development-tools/pre-push-checks).
- Do not manually bump `TUTURUUU_PLATFORM_VERSION`, package versions, or
  changelogs — Release Please owns version updates.

### Testing

- Tests run with Vitest. Use `bun test` for the full suite or filter to a single
  workspace (for example `bun --filter @tuturuuu/web test`).
- Write unit tests for utilities and cover error scenarios.
- Run focused tests before the full `bun validate` gate.

### Performance

- Default to server-side rendering and Server Components where possible.
- Use TanStack Query for client-side fetching and caching; avoid `useEffect` for
  data fetching.
- Minimize bundle size and profile performance regularly.

## Tools and Scripts

### Package Management

Dependencies are always installed from inside the owning workspace — never by
hand-editing the root `package.json` and never with a `--workspace` flag.

```bash
# Install all dependencies
bun install

# Add a dependency to an app (e.g. apps/web)
cd apps/web && bun add <package>

# Add a dependency to a shared package (e.g. packages/ui)
cd packages/ui && bun add <package>

# Update dependencies within their current ranges
bun update-all

# Upgrade workspace dependencies to the latest releases, including major versions
bun update --latest --recursive
```

For a broad refresh, also update Rust (`cargo update` in `apps/backend`), Python
(`uv lock --upgrade` in `apps/discord`), and Flutter
(`flutter pub upgrade --major-versions` in `apps/mobile`). Keep native CocoaPods
locks aligned with Flutter plugins and retain stable versions when a registry's
`latest` tag points at a prerelease. The configured npm release-age policy still
applies. Run `bun check:changed` locally and require `bun validate` and affected
app builds to pass in CI for the exact commit.

Keep React and React DOM aligned at 19.2.8 while React Three Fiber 9.7.0
requires versions below 19.3. The root overrides also prevent transitive peer
dependencies from selecting a second runtime; revisit both overrides and
Hive workspace constraints when Fiber supports the next React minor. Keep
`@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` on the matching runtime minor as well.
Other packages retain compatible consumer ranges so the repository overrides do
not force a second React copy into published-package consumers.

For a security patch, save the initial `bun audit --json` result and update direct
dependencies with `bun update <package>@<fixed-version>` from the owning workspace.
For transitive fixes, manage the root `overrides` with
`bun pm pkg set --json 'overrides=<merged JSON object>'`, preserving existing
entries. Prefer selectors restricted to vulnerable versions, with the minimum
fixed release on each major; test the consumer before crossing a major version.
Re-run the audit after resolution because an initial fix can itself have a newer
advisory. Verify the resulting lock with `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, run
focused tests through the resource queue, and require applicable exact-commit CI.
Builds remain CI-only, and paused runtimes remain excluded.

Keep Vite+ and its core alias on the same published version; check the upstream
release's bundled Vite version separately from plain `vite` dependencies.
Audit Python locks, Flutter/Pub advisories, and pinned Actions separately from Bun.
An advisory without a published fix remains an explicit blocker, even when other
packages are clean. Do not remove a used dependency or suppress an advisory merely
to reduce the reported count.

React-PDF 11 requires Node.js 22.13 or newer; CI uses Node.js 24. Its default
Suspense behavior differs from version 10, so the shared PDF viewer explicitly
keeps its existing loading and error handling with `suspense={false}`. Mermaid 12
also changes visual defaults; the chat renderers set `layout: 'dagre'` and
`look: 'classic'` to preserve existing diagrams.

### Development Commands

```bash
# Start all apps
bun dev

# Start a specific app
bun dev:web

# Run tests (Vitest)
bun test

# Run the full verification gate before a PR
bun validate
```

### Database Commands

```bash
# Start the local Supabase stack
bun sb:start

# Create a new migration
bun sb:new

# Apply pending migrations locally
bun sb:up

# Generate TypeScript types from the local schema
bun sb:typegen

# Reset the local database (re-runs all migrations + seeds)
bun sb:reset
```

<Warning>
  `bun sb:push` and `bun sb:linkpush` push migrations to the **remote**
  Supabase project and are reserved for the maintainer applying production
  changes. Do not run them — prepare migrations locally with `bun sb:up` and let
  the user apply production changes.
</Warning>

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

1. **Build / Check Failures**: Run `bun check:changed` to surface TypeScript and Biome errors in changed files, and confirm dependencies are installed with `bun install`
2. **Database Issues**: Ensure the local Supabase stack is running (`bun sb:start`) and migrations are applied (`bun sb:up`)
3. **Test Failures**: Check environment setup and re-run the focused Vitest workspace before `bun check:changed`; the full `bun validate` gate runs in CI
4. **Performance Issues**: Use React DevTools and bundle analyzers

### Getting Help

- Check existing documentation
- Search GitHub issues
- Ask in team channels
- Create detailed bug reports

## Contributing

When contributing to the platform:

1. Read the relevant documentation
2. Follow the established patterns
3. Write tests for new features
4. Update documentation
5. Submit a pull request with a clear description

### Task-owned temporary files for check stages

When an admitted runner has a constrained `/tmp` user quota, prepare a unique,
existing current-user directory with mode `0700` on a filesystem with freshly
verified quota and free-space capacity. Set `TUTURUUU_CHECK_CHILD_TMPDIR` to its
absolute real path when invoking normal `bun validate` through `ttr resources run`.
The option changes `TMPDIR`, `TMP`, and `TEMP` only for validation children.
Keep the check runner's own `TMPDIR`, `HOME`, and `TTR_RESOURCES_HOME` unchanged;
both shared queues remain in their original locations. Directory validation
alone does not establish capacity or authorize cleanup.

Invalid directories fail without falling back to `/tmp`. Child processes carry
a sentinel preserved through Turbo strict mode that rejects a nested `bun validate`
CLI before it creates a queue;
imports of the check module remain allowed. Run another broad check separately
through the original queues. This option does not skip checks, change resource
limits, or turn an incomplete or failing check into a pass.

## Aggregate validation and native Bun type checking

`bun validate` is the repository aggregate (formerly the custom `bun check`
script). `bun validate:now` retains the explicit `--force-now` queue behavior.
Both invoke the same `scripts/check.js`; flags, fail-fast handling, mandatory
Biome follow-through, queues and child-temp isolation are unchanged. The legacy
`tuturuuu-bun-check` queue directory and environment names stay stable so old
and new runner processes coordinate during the rename.

The aggregate still covers workspace tests, Turbo type-checking, blocking Biome
format/lint, source size, public SEO, server console, internal-app-auth, satellite
cookie auth, offline Worker wiring, multi-account vault ownership, legacy API
wrappers, mobile iOS settings and API mappings, script tests, next-intl setup,
translation validity/key parity/sorting/namespaces and migration timestamps.
Platform release alignment runs for release files; Discord Python validation
runs for Discord changes. No component was replaced with a type-only command.
`bun check:changed` remains the separate build-free pre-push gate; other
`check:*` commands retain their roles.

`ttr resources run -- bun check --no-script -p <project>` explicitly invokes Bun's native type-only
checker. A package script named `check` takes precedence over native checking;
`scripts/validate-command.test.js` rejects that name in the root and every
workspace, including retained inactive workspaces. The test is discovered by
the existing script-test gate. Native checking is not a substitute for
`bun validate`, app builds, guards, tests, or declaration generation. The ban on
local aggregate/build execution applies to `bun validate`; native qualification
still requires resource admission and a bounded thread count. The resource wrapper
injects `--threads=<lane buildJobs>` when absent and clamps explicit values to
that lane limit, preserving smaller requests. The aggregate rejects unknown arguments, including `--help` and
`--dry-run`, before starting work, prints one usage line to stderr and exits 1; neither flag
provides an aggregate preview.

The inventory recognizes both `wrangler types` and `cf types` as declaration
generators, including scripts with custom names. It reads package manifests
without executing generators. The legacy detector and its data-only regression
fixture have an explicit `producer-inventory` Wrangler-gap admission.

### Native checker qualification

The required gate remains `tsc` 7.0.2, including `run-tsc-build.js` and its
cache invalidation. PR #6468 supplies optional tsrs 7.1-dev shadow/advisory pre-push
comparison; it is not the required CI baseline. Keep both until a replacement
proves all existing semantics. Do not remove TypeScript: declaration producers
and editor tooling still require it. Bun 1.4.4 reports TypeScript 7.0.2 through
`bun -p process.versions.typescript`, matching the repository compiler version.
It embeds its own compiler and standard library; matching versions alone is not
proof of diagnostic or build equivalence. The repository Bun pin remains owned
by the separate Bun upgrade/security lane; this change does not update it.
Native execution requires Bun 1.4.4, while `validate` works with the existing pin. See [Bun's native checker](https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/check).

There are 89 root/workspace manifests; only the root defined `check` before
the rename. Active scripts invoke `tsc` from TypeScript 7.0.2, often through
`run-tsc-build.js`. No active manifest invokes a separate `tsgo` binary; that
name is recognized by the changed-files project resolver. tsrs is installed
externally for shadow/pre-push use, not as a workspace dependency.

Run `node scripts/ci/bun-check-inventory.js` to inventory root/workspace scripts,
resolved type-check projects, inactive workspaces and custom emit/generation
producers. Turbo's `type-check` still depends on `^build` and `^type-check`.
Meet has a custom declaration producer; Calendar/Mail split app, boundary and
Worker configs; several services generate Wrangler ambient declarations before
checking. Those steps must survive any future switch.

The opt-in Linux harness is `scripts/ci/bun-check-qualification.js --out <private-dir>
--threads 6 --runs 5 [--tsrs <pinned-binary>]`. Invoke it with `node` inside the
existing fenced exact-SHA runner after frozen dependency installation. It does
not create another CI gate. Each report records source SHA, lock hash, versions,
host/load, exact commands, resolved configs/references, file closures and hashes,
full diagnostics, exit status, wall time and peak RSS. `--all` disables native
diagnostic grouping. The known-invalid control adds a fresh `TS2322` assignment
under `packages/types/src`, requires every checker to report it, and removes the
file in `finally`; the mutation and source hash are recorded separately.

This harness compares the same **no-emit projection** used by the existing
shadow: `noEmit=true`, `incremental=false`, `composite=false`. This alone does
not prove the original build/reference/emit semantics. First runs are process
cold; subsequent runs use fresh processes with warm OS caches. It does not evict
shared host caches or claim cold filesystem results. Alternate checker order,
report all five observations and errors, and compare diagnostic multisets before
comparing performance. Real diagnostic differences or unverified generated
closures prohibit gate promotion. Preserve declaration/emit tasks even after
future diagnostic equivalence is established.

### Bun 1.4.4 evaluation: initial declaration closure

The first exact-source run at `b56c8fde67b487ee07961004feb92930f121b945`
used a Linux build host (x86_64, 20 CPUs), the fenced
`early-merge-validate.sh` runner, Bun 1.4.4 and Node 24.22.1. Both Bun's embedded
compiler and the baseline reported TypeScript 7.0.2; the tsrs pin reported
7.1.0-dev.20260930.4. The frozen `bun.lock` SHA256 was
`c4687dadb08c5aa33a132d860f8d44a0b7ee2c032ec11c09e5724a4d864999e2`.

All checkers used a six-thread budget (`--threads 6`, `GOMAXPROCS=6`,
`RAYON_NUM_THREADS=6` as applicable). The four standard Types/Supabase/Internal
API/Masonry declaration prerequisites were built first. Each paired comparison
used identical source/dependencies and effective no-emit flags; all 11 recorded
input closure hashes stayed unchanged. There was one process-cold pass and four
warm passes per checker, with alternating order, plus five error-control runs.
The host was shared (initial load averages 9.57/34.93/31.40); these are
observations, not an adoption or speedup claim. Source-loading inventory had
already warmed filesystem caches before the first timed compiler process.

| Checker | Process-cold total, s | Warm total median [range], s | Error median [range], s | Peak RSS, MiB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tsc | 38.295 | 37.336 [37.112-37.599] | 0.231 [0.227-0.240] | 7855.8 |
| bun | 7.337 | 7.346 [7.206-7.493] | 0.071 [0.067-0.072] | 2159.9 |
| tsrs | 6.520 | 6.216 [6.100-6.310] | 0.066 [0.063-0.072] | 2418.1 |

Totals above sum the 11 project checks sequentially. Peak RSS is the maximum
single checker process, not summed memory. Warm values summarize four totals;
error values summarize five runs of the injected Types control only. tsrs and
Bun did not perform identical validation work on this initial closure, so the
timing columns must not be used as an equivalence-adjusted performance ratio.

| Project | tsc / Bun / tsrs diagnostics | Bun exact parity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/types/tsconfig.build.json` | 0 / 0 / 0 | yes |
| `packages/utils/tsconfig.typecheck.json` | 0 / 0 / 0 | yes |
| `packages/ui/tsconfig.typecheck.json` | 0 / 0 / 20 | yes |
| `packages/supabase/tsconfig.typecheck.json` | 0 / 0 / 0 | yes |
| `packages/internal-api/tsconfig.typecheck.json` | 0 / 0 / 0 | yes |
| `apps/tasks/tsconfig.json` | 0 / 0 / 0 | yes |
| `apps/calendar/tsconfig.json` | 0 / 0 / 0 | yes |
| `apps/calendar/tsconfig.worker.json` | 1 / 1 / 1 | yes |
| `apps/meet/tsconfig.app.json` | 0 / 0 / 0 | yes |
| `apps/meet/tsconfig.cloudflare.json` | 2 / 0 / 2 | NO |
| `apps/web/tsconfig.json` | 2 / 2 / 20 | yes |

Every checker reported the injected `TS2322` at the same file, line, column and
message in all five runs; the control was removed afterward. Existing real
checkout diagnostics also matched exactly: Calendar Worker reported `TS2307`
for the absent generated `#calendar-handler` alias, and Web plus SDK reported
`TS2307` for absent `@tuturuuu/devbox` declarations. These are genuine checkout
diagnostics, but they are missing generated inputs rather than evidence of a
fully prepared production type gate.

Meet's Worker config has `disableSourceOfProjectReferenceRedirect: true` and
references its app declaration producer. With those declarations absent, tsc
reported two `TS6305` diagnostics for `token.d.ts` and `handler.d.ts`; Bun
reported none. This is consistent with Bun's documented use of referenced
source instead of prebuilt declarations. Removing the current gate at this point
would lose an existing generated-output assertion. tsrs also differed from the
7.0.2 baseline (20 UI diagnostics and 20 Web diagnostics versus 0 and 2).
**Native gate promotion remains unqualified.** Retain the authoritative
producers, emit/declaration validation and existing baseline.

The follow-up uses `--all-projects --runs 1` after running the existing complete
Turbo type gate, including Meet/Calendar boundary producers, to distinguish
missing-output differences from source diagnostic differences. This mode covers
all active inventoried projects and expands Meet's solution root into its two
concrete configs; inactive TanStack remains excluded. It is coverage evidence,
not a second performance benchmark or an automatic rollout decision.

### Prepared-closure coverage result

At `612429d21223b91018e632ebd84b6044c19d00ec`, the unchanged authoritative
Turbo type graph passed on the same Linux host (72 seconds, concurrency 2,
`GOMAXPROCS=6`). Its declaration and boundary producers prepared the complete
closure. The subsequent one-pass comparison covered **86 concrete configs from
79 active workspaces**: all had exact diagnostic parity, zero diagnostics and
unchanged input-closure hashes. The additional TS2322 negative control also
matched exactly and failed in both checkers as intended. The lock hash and
compiler versions matched the earlier run. Inactive TanStack was not executed.

This qualifies the observed **prepared no-emit projection** of those configs.
It does not establish drop-in equivalence for the complete current gate:
`composite`/incremental behavior was disabled for the paired measurements,
Bun intentionally does not enforce the same missing-reference-output behavior,
and it does not provide emit or the existing producer/cache receipts. Keep the
TypeScript gate and tsrs shadow; no checker dependency was removed. Before a
switch, compare unmodified config semantics and preserve the producer/output
assertions explicitly, including a missing/stale-output regression. Do not
interpret the prepared all-green result as permission to discard those checks.

The complete build-free pre-push gate passed on Linux for the implementation
commit, including the changed SDK/Devbox tests and type checks; focused Node
coverage passed 92 tests on the Mac through resource admission. The installed
Mac shim and nested workspace CLI had incompatible admission behavior, so that
owned full-gate invocation was stopped and the remaining checks ran on Linux.
No installed scheduler was modified. Exact-head hosted CI and independent
review remain separate delivery gates; no merge or production sync is part of
this change.
